measure_as_declared: "Share of true nulls with p under 0.05 and under 0.01"
applies_in: every scenario; every design, no RUV included ("applied to every arm, arm 1 included")
stated_source: "Bradley 1978, through secondary sources: the liberal band 0.025 to 0.075 at 0.05". The original was not read; the band is two-sided and the rule applies its upper limit only. No source is stated for 0.015 at the 0.01 level
reading_and_amendments: A1: the null rate is a mean over data sets with its Monte Carlo standard error (mean plus qnorm(0.975) standard errors), not a pooled binomial over tests. Pass when both upper bounds are within their limits; fail when either lower bound is above its limit

measure_as_declared: "mean false discovery proportion among the package's calls (q under 0.05)"
applies_in: every scenario; every design, no RUV included
stated_source: independent review R-02: "Bound the mean false discovery proportion absolutely (upper bound at most 0.075)". No literature source is stated for the limit
reading_and_amendments: A1: a mean over data sets, normal bound. Under the global null the proportion of a data set is 0 or 1, so the mean is the share of data sets with any call

rule_as_declared: Share of runs with false discovery proportion above 0.10
limit_as_declared: upper bound at most the true-factor arm's share plus 0.05
measure_as_declared: "share of runs with a false discovery proportion above 0.10"
applies_in: every scenario; every design, no RUV included
stated_source: independent review R-03: "A per-run rule (share of runs above 10%, against the true-factor arm plus a margin)", naming Efron 2007 and Leek and Storey 2008
reading_and_amendments: A2: the limit is the true-factor design's point share in the same scenario and feature subset plus 0.05, not its bound; exact (Clopper-Pearson) bound for the share. Lipidomics/metabolomics: one proportion per data set over both assays, in the design and in the limit alike

rule_as_declared: Gain, in cells with a factor
limit_as_declared: lower bound of the power gain over no RUV above 0, or of the reduction in rule 3's share above 0
measure_as_declared: "power"; "share of runs with a false discovery proportion above 0.10"
applies_in: scenarios with an unwanted factor: all but the three without one (A10; a known batch beside the factor counts as a factor)
stated_source: independent review R-03: "rule 3 becomes a gain over no-RUV"
reading_and_amendments: A3: paired by data set against no RUV, normal bounds on the differences; no RUV has a gain of exactly 0 and so fails by construction. A4: fail when both upper bounds are at most 0. A12: in the global-null scenario the power gain is undefined and, where no RUV makes almost no false calls, no design can show a reduction, so every design fails there, the true-factor design included; both readings (literal; that scenario judged without rule 4) are scored and the choice was put to the user (revision 1.4)

rule_as_declared: No harm, in cells without a factor
limit_as_declared: upper bound of the power loss against no RUV at most 0.02
applies_in: the scenarios without an unwanted factor (one main, two extra-hard; A10)
stated_source: "Rule 5 is a stated judgement. Fitting two extra factors at 6 per group costs about 0.02 power by arithmetic, so a design that always removes two cannot pass it; one that can return k = 0 can." (independent review R-04)
reading_and_amendments: paired by data set against no RUV, normal bound; fail when the lower bound is above 0.02

measure_as_declared: "designed refusals and crashes, counted apart. A refused run is scored as its no-RUV result"
applies_in: every scenario; every design, no RUV included
stated_source: independent review R-07: exact binomial bounds; "refusals counted apart and scored as no-RUV results". No literature source is stated for the limit
reading_and_amendments: A7: a crashed data set has no measures, is left out of the other rules and is counted here. A6 and revision 1.3: a refusal, by the package's design or by a comparator method's own stop (RUVinv at 3 per group or with 5 internal standards), is not a crash and carries the data set's no-RUV result

rule_as_declared: Global null (C4): share of runs with any call
measure_as_declared: "the share of runs with any call, beside arm 1's"
applies_in: the global-null scenario only; every design (A11)
stated_source: independent review R-09: "add a 0% true-effects cell at full group size; compare with arm 1". No source is stated for the limit
reading_and_amendments: exact (Clopper-Pearson) bound. Not available in lipidomics/metabolomics, where the global-null scenario is void

limit_as_declared: "One-sided 97.5% bounds; exact binomial bounds for shares."
measure_as_declared: "each with its Monte Carlo standard error over runs"
stated_source: Morris, White, Crowther 2019 (Monte Carlo standard errors); independent review R-07 (Clopper-Pearson)
reading_and_amendments: A1: exact bounds for shares of data sets (rules 3, 6, 7); mean plus or minus qnorm(0.975) Monte Carlo standard errors for means over data sets and paired differences (rules 1, 2, 4, 5)

limit_as_declared: "A cell where the true-factor arm fails rules 1 or 2 is void and reported."
measure_as_declared: rules 1 and 2 of the true-factor design
stated_source: independent review R-06: "void cells the true-factor arm does not pass"
reading_and_amendments: A5: "fails" means the whole interval outside the limit; a true-factor design that is only inconclusive is flagged, not void. Revision 1.3, before the confirming runs: the technical-duplicate scenario in transcriptomics and in lipidomics/metabolomics is reported, not used to judge. Void as scored among the main scenarios: the global null in lipidomics/metabolomics (rule 2)

limit_as_declared: "Pass: every rule in every core cell. Fail: some bound in a core cell outside its limit with the whole interval outside. Inconclusive: otherwise. Stress cells never fail a design: they give its conditions of use (for example a minimum group size)."
applies_in: main ("core") scenarios that are not void; extra-hard ("stress") scenarios give conditions of use only
stated_source: independent review R-06: "core cells (must pass) and stress cells (state conditions)"
reading_and_amendments: A4: the interval is the two one-sided 97.5% bounds. A8: each design is judged on all features and on the features complete in every sample; the summary uses its primary subset. A14: "every core cell" was read as every main scenario in which the design runs, so the technical-replicate designs, run in one scenario, pass on that scenario alone; whether that makes a design eligible was put to the user. A12: see rule 4
